summary: Willamette lookout site on Fuji Mountain, Lane County: fire finder 1919, cabin 1926-1928, R-6 cabin 1959, burned or removed 1968; now a former lookout summit.

facts.design: R-6 ground cabin (1959), replacing an earlier cupola cabin
facts.status_note: The cabin burned in 1968 per the register and firelookout.com; the Rex's page gives August 26, 1968 as the removal date.

access.note: Reached by a short out-and-back hike from the Upper Trailhead on FR 5883. The summit is a former fire lookout site, not a standing tower.

visit.trail_note: Drive FR 5883 to the Upper Trailhead (about 10.5 miles, potholed for the first mile), then hike out and back to the summit.

events.note: Established as a tent camp and fire finder stand; an alidade established to locate fires
Edgar Buchanan was lookout on Fuji for the summer
D-6 cab erected per the register; a September 1926 item reported two lookout houses built, one on Fuji
firelookout.com dates a cupola cabin to 1928
Orlo Flock heading to the summer lookout station on Fuji
Inspection asked whether lightning protection on old lookout houses should be brought up to standard; Fuji was the example
R-6 ground cabin built, replacing the earlier cabin
Lookout cabin burned, nine years after the 1959 cabin
Rex's Fire Lookout Page gives August 26, 1968 as the date the lookout house was removed
Registered with Former Fire Lookout Sites on April 25, 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says a D-6 cab was erected in 1926. A September 1926 item reports two lookout houses built, one on Fuji, and a January 1927 item says one was placed on Fuji. firelookout.com says a cupola cabin was built in 1928. The story gives all three.

The register and firelookout.com say the cabin burned in 1968. The Rex's page gives August 26, 1968 as the date the lookout house was removed. The story says the register and firelookout.com both report a burn in 1968 and notes the Rex's removal date.

notes_for_editor: The brief record (R-6, 1959 cabin, 1968 end, 2011 registration) is supported. The brief lists the agency as 'U.S.Forest Service'; the register's page spells it that way too, so no correction is proposed. The 360cities summit panorama, which describes the 1968 removal, returned 403 and was not read. Oregon Hikers is the only read source on the summit today; it does not describe any remains. Dates for the first cabin disagree across three sources and the story does not pick one.
